# Cross-Exchange Liquidity Commentary – 2026-08-04

The liquidity hierarchy divides clearly into three tiers. NYSE and Nasdaq 100 dominate as tier-one venues, with NYSE posting the lowest ILLIQ cost at 0.0059% per $1M traded despite a wider 0.6619% AR spread, while Nasdaq 100 offers exceptional tightness at 0.0024% per $1M traded and superior comparable volume of $427.4M. The mid-tier comprises Tokyo, Euronext, SIX Swiss, Hong Kong, and London, where Tokyo stands out with the highest turnover ratio at 3.0028% despite moderate ILLIQ of 0.0352% per $1M, whereas Euronext combines the tightest AR spread at 0.5297% with modest ILLIQ of 0.0294% per $1M—a rare metric divergence suggesting strong algo-driven execution quality. London Stock Exchange underperforms this tier, exhibiting elevated ILLIQ of 0.0803% per $1M and the widest AR spread at 0.8061% among mid-rank venues. The laggard tier—Xetra and Korea Exchange—show deteriorating liquidity profiles, with Korea Exchange displaying the poorest metrics across the board: ILLIQ of 0.1607% per $1M, a 1.5216% AR spread, and minimal comparable volume of $18.0M, signaling structural fragmentation or reduced institutional participation in Korean equities.
